newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-PUTT TRY SETS UP NATAL VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-PUTT TRY SETS UP NATAL VICTORY.

text.p: A 78th-minute try from Natal scrum-half Kevin Putt allowed his side to steal a 28-23 victory over New South Wales in a thunderous Super 12 encounter at Kings Park on Saturday.

Natal's third win in the competition, following their surprise defeat at the hands of Free State last weekend, moved them into joint second place in the table alongside Australian Capital Territory on 16 points.
But the home side had to withstand a bruising onslaught from the NSW Waratahs on a warm evening which produced rugby of a furious pace.
Determined play - and tries from left wing David Campese and centre Richard Tombs - had given New South Wales a deserved 23-18 lead with 10 minutes remaining.
But Natal reduced the deficit to 23-21 when the faultless boot of full-back Gavin Lawless landed his seventh successful kick out of seven, paving the way for Putt's decisive try.

An athletic lineout take from Springbok lock Mark Andrews set up a forward drive and the livewire scrum-half was on hand from the ensuing ruck to thread his way across the line for Natal's only try of the match. Lawless added the conversion for a match tally of 23 points.
The Waratahs, who now have just one win and six points from their opening four games, had to settle for a solitary bonus point for finishing within seven points of Natal.

It was tough on their heavier pack who took only six minutes to set up a try for the inspirational Campese, playing his last match on South African soil, who slipped through the Natal defence unchallenged to score under the posts.
Campese, who was given a yellow card in the second half for swearing at referee Tappe Henning, said afterwards it had been a tough game for both sides.

"The ball was a bit slippery, temperatures must have been around 30 degrees and I guess Natal just wanted it a little more than us at the end. Some of the refereeing interpretations were strange, though, and that made it difficult when both sides wanted to play a quick game."

Natal - Gavin Lawless; Joos Joubert, Jeremy Thomson, Geoff Appleford, Cabous van der Westhuizen; Henry Honiball, Kevin Putt; Gary Teichmann (captain), Wickus van Heerden (Dieter Kriese, 71st), Wayne Fyvie, Mark Andrews, John Slade, Adrian Garvey, JohnAllan, Ollie le Roux (Rob Kempson 66th).

New South Wales - Matt Burke; Alistair Murdoch, Graeme Bond, Richard Tombs, David Campese; Scott Bowen, Sam Payne; Fili Finau, Stuart Pinkerton, Michael Brial (Daniel Manu 55th), Sam Domoni, Tim Gavin (captain), Andrew Blades, Mark Bell (Phil Kearns 3rd), Richard Harry.
